name: limit_three_points_in_a_row
why: Three points in a line do not make a plane: infinitely many pass through a line. SOLIDWORKS answers null and does not say why -- measured. Here we refuse BEFORE calling, because the why is known without asking: the cross product of the two vectors is zero. A refusal that explains is worth as much as one that guesses the reason afterwards.
_why_letting_solidworks_fail_is_not_enou: The message that would come out would be «the plane was not created and SOLIDWORKS does not say why», which is true and useless. Whoever got a number wrong would not know which of the three.

expect.tolerance_why: three points on the plane z=0: the normal is the Z axis
expect.why: MOVING THE THIRD POINT TEN MILLIMETRES OFF THE LINE, the plane is born. It is the half that says the refusal above looks at the alignment and not at something else: it changes a single number out of nine.
and after the refusal the planes were still three: the refused step had left none along the way
